finding.claim: iconUrl is stored without any validation and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync job, allowing SSRF to internal hosts, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary URLs. Unlike webhookUrl, there is no scheme or host check.
finding.source: `icon` parameter of PUT /profile, handled in Profile.update()
finding.sink: HttpClient.send() with HttpRequest built from URI.create(iconUrl) (GET)

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives the attacker-controlled icon
this.iconUrl = icon, stored with no validation
nightly sync() job runs later on the stored value
URI.create(iconUrl) is fetched via c.send(GET), and the response body is read as bytes

finding.guards_checked: The regex check at line 12 applies only to the webhook parameter, not to icon. There is no scheme allowlist, host allowlist, or private/link-local IP blocking for iconUrl. The HttpClient is passed in, so its redirect policy and proxy settings are unknown, but nothing on this path restricts the target.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the request-supplied `icon` unvalidated (the regex at :12 covers only `webhook`), and sync() fetches it at :23 via URI.create(iconUrl) with GET and reads the body as bytes.
